description: Fifteen gilyonot, five passages, thirty years. Choose a passage, choose a year, and read it through her sources and questions.
shows: The flagship. More than forty sources, and pages of the Leningrad Codex that zoom to the line under discussion. Every quote of Nechama’s cites the sheet it came from.

description: Fifteen gilyonot, five passages, thirty years. Choose a passage, choose a year, and read it through her sources and questions.
shows: Built the same way as Bereshit, from her original scans. Questions the online digitization dropped or changed are restored, and her own comparison tables sit side by side in the panel.

title.en: Parshat Nasso — A Garden of Forking Paths

description: Twenty-eight gilyonot, four themes, thirty years of return. Choose a theme, choose her angle, walk the sheet.
shows: The second garden, built the same way. It branches by theme rather than by passage, then by the angle she took in a given year. It shows the method carrying from one parsha to the next.

description: Visiting the Iniquity of Parents upon Children — Exodus 20:5
shows: One gilayon, read start to finish. When the sheet turns on two verses that seem to contradict each other, Exodus 20:5 and Deuteronomy 24:16, they appear side by side.

description: Over and over and over: from Jacob's deathbed to the morning Shema, every generation chooses the covenant again.
shows: A theme sheet, not a single passage. It moves from Genesis to the siddur, changing the pinned verse at every stop and lighting the words that come back each time: a gathering, a covenant scroll read aloud, an age of 110.

title.en: Learning to Read Midrash: King and Warrior

description: How a mashal works — a six-step reading of the Tanhuma's parable on “Take, please” (Genesis 22:2)
shows: English-first. A chapter of a published book by a contemporary teacher, walking through the author’s six-step method for reading a mashal.

description: A guided close reading of Pirkei Avot 1:11 — oldest layers to modern voices
shows: Built from a single Mishnah instead of an existing sheet. Four readings of “evil waters,” from the oldest to the newest.

description: The authority of custom in Jewish law — Talmud Pesachim
shows: Talmud, not Torah. The Bavli and the Yerushalmi read against each other, from a Pardes Institute sheet.

retired: Early single-gilayon prototype; Yitro covers the format and Bereshit supersedes the method.
